passages.original: ἦ που νῦν ἅπασα μὲν ποίησις ἀπήνθηκε, πᾶσα δὲ συγγραφὴ συνέσταλται, πάντα δʼ ὑπολέλοιπε τὸν ἐξηγητὴν καὶ προστάτην οὐκ ἔχοντα, χήρα δʼ ἡ τέχνη. συνέσταλται δʼ ἀναγκαίως μικρὰ μικρῶς τοῖς πολλοῖς. ὃ δέ φησιν Ἀριστοφάνης περὶ Αἰσχύλου σκότον εἶναι τεθνηκότος, τοῦτʼ ἄξιον καὶ περὶ τούτου νῦν εἰπεῖν
passages.english: Surely now all poetry has lost its bloom, all prose-writing has shrunk, and everything has been left behind without its interpreter and champion, and the art is widowed. And it has necessarily shrunk, small things in a small way for the many. What Aristophanes says about Aeschylus, that there is darkness now that he is dead, is fitting to say now about this man too.
passages.notes: xtlg0284 is probably Aelius Aristides; this appears to be his funeral oration for the grammarian Alexander of Cotiaeum. The phrase μικρὰ μικρῶς τοῖς πολλοῖς is obscure and may be corrupt; the rendering 'small things in a small way for the many' is literal and its sense uncertain. The Aristophanes allusion is presumably to Frogs, though the wording given here does not match a known line exactly.
